evidence: books/store-log-damage.lisp:157-160: `(defun fn-lgdm-entry-len (h ps extent) ... (let ((n (ec-call (fn-lg-declared-len h)))) (and (natp n) (<= n (nfix (- (nfix extent) (fn-lgdm-q ps)))) n)))`; same in books/store-log-stream.lisp:103-106 (fn-lgw-entry-len). Host: io.lisp:6560 `(e (and n (fnn-octet-list (fnn-log-pread fd q (fnn-nat n)))))` and io.lisp:6611 `(e (if n (fnn-log-pread fd pos (fnn-nat n)) ...))`. The valid bound is known at this point: fn-lg-open-bound (store-log.lisp:394-398) is MAX for kind 1/3 and only kind 2 may reach *fn-frame-max-payload*.
fix: Bound the declared length before reading. Return NIL from fn-lgw-entry-len/fn-lgdm-entry-len when the header's kind is 1 or 3 and n exceeds MAX+overhead (and for kind 3, the rotation entry's fixed size). For kind 2, read and validate incrementally, or at least refuse lengths above the batch bound OMAX. In the probe, keep the entry in the octet buffer stobj as the stream does instead of building an octet list.
reviewer: fn-lg-declared-len (store-log.lisp:369-376) checks only the 'FNLG' magic and then returns overhead plus the u32 length. fn-lgdm-entry-len (store-log-damage.lisp:157-160) and fn-lgw-entry-len (store-log-stream.lisp:103-106) cap that only by the remaining extent. The host preads that many octets: io.lisp:6618 in the walk, and io.lisp:6560 in the probe, which also listifies them. A bit flip in the length field of a real header therefore reads up to min(4 GiB, the rest of the extent). The tighter bound fn-lg-open-bound (store-log.lisp:394-398) is applied only after the read. Payload octets that contain FNLG headers at probe strides do make the probe do this repeatedly, but only after a tear or other damage.
scenario: Case 1: one bit flips in the u32 length field of an entry header at the stop (or a torn batch leaves an 'FNLG' header with a garbage length). The open then preads up to the rest of the segment, possibly GiBs, into one array. In the probe that array is then turned into an ACL2 octet list at about 16 bytes per octet. Case 2: a client article whose body carries 'FNLG' headers at 4096-octet strides is part of a batch that tears in a crash. Every such stride makes the probe read and listify up to extent-q octets. The open can exhaust the heap instead of returning the named :damaged/:torn verdict.
title: Log stream and damage probe read whatever length an unvalidated header declares, up to the remaining extent, before checking it against the record bound
